newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam, Japan defence chiefs seek to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam, Japan defence chiefs seek to boost ties.

text.p: Japan's Deputy Defence Minister met defence chiefs in Vietnam last week to exchange views on policy and discuss issues of mutual concern, official media reports said on Monday.
Naoaki Murata, the Japan Defence Agency's highest-ranking career official, met his Vietnamese counterpart and then Defence Minister General Doan Khue during a three-day visit to Hanoi.

"Khue...said this visit, as well as recent contacts between officers from the two countries' defence bodies would help the Japanese and Vietnamese armies better understand one another, thus helping further develop the friendly and cooperative ties between the two peoples," the Vietnam News Agency said.
No details of the meetings were given, though Japanese officials said Hanoi and Tokyo planned to strengthen links between their military forces.
Murata, on a Southeast Asia tour that includes Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore, left Vietnam on Saturday.
His tour followed a swing through the region earlier this month by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, who is keen to broaden Tokyo's relations with Southeast Asian nations.
